The blue-uniformed conductor, with a lantern under his arm, and his punch in hand, entered the smoking-car of the Boston express. arxiv-1806-10771.title: Rich Character-Level Information for Korean Morphological Analysis and Part-of-Speech Tagging
arxiv-1806-10771.creator: Andrew Matteson, Chanhee Lee, Heuiseok Lim
arxiv-1806-10771.description: Abstract Due to the fact that Korean is a highly agglutinative, character-rich language, previous work on Korean morphological analysis typically employs the use of sub-character features known as graphemes or otherwise utilizes comprehensive prior linguistic knowledge (i.e., a dictionary of known morphological transformation forms, or actions).

arxiv-2304-09874.creator: Muskaan Chopra γ \gamma , * , Prakash Chandra Chhipa δ \delta , * , Gopal Mengi γ \gamma , * , Varun Gupta γ \gamma and Marcus Liwicki δ \delta δ \delta Machine Learning Group, EISLAB, Luleå Tekniska Universitet, Luleå, Sweden { prakash.chandra.chhipa, marcus.liwicki } @ltu.se γ \gamma Chandigarh Co
arxiv-2304-09874.description: Abstract This work presents a novel domain adaption paradigm for studying contrastive self-supervised representation learning and knowledge transfer using remote sensing satellite data. Major state-of-the-art remote sensing visual domain efforts primarily focus on fully supervised learning approaches that rely entirely on human annotations.

arxiv-2306-10188.title: Mutual Interference Mitigation in PMCW Automotive Radar † \dagger First two authors have equal contributions. This work was sponsored by the National Science Foundation Grant ECCS-1809225.
arxiv-2306-10188.creator: Zahra Esmaeilbeig #1 † \dagger , Arindam Bose *2 † \dagger , Mojtaba Soltanalian #3
arxiv-2306-10188.description: Abstract This paper addresses the challenge of mutual interference in phase-modulated continuous wave (PMCW) millimeter-wave (mmWave) automotive radar systems. The increasing demand for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) has led to a proliferation of vehicles equipped with mmWave radar systems that operate in the same frequency band, resulting in mutual interference that can degrade radar performance creating safety hazards.

arxiv-2406-01233.title: Multi-word Term Embeddings Improve Lexical Product Retrieval
arxiv-2406-01233.description: Abstract Product search is uniquely different from search for documents, Internet resources or vacancies, therefore it requires the development of specialized search systems. The present work describes the H1 embdedding model, designed for an offline term indexing of product descriptions at e-commerce platforms.

arxiv-2410-03775.title: Beyond Correlation: The Impact of Human Uncertainty in Measuring the Effectiveness of Automatic Evaluation and LLM-as-a-Judge
arxiv-2410-03775.creator: Aparna Elangovan, Lei Xu, Jongwoo Ko, Mahsa Elyasi, Ling Liu Sravan Bodapati Dan Roth
arxiv-2410-03775.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Aparna Elangovan, Lei Xu, Jongwoo Ko, Mahsa Elyasi, Ling Liu Sravan Bodapati Dan Roth. The effectiveness of automatic evaluation of generative models is typically measured by comparing the labels generated via automation with labels by humans using correlation metrics. However, metrics like Krippendorff’s α \alpha and Randolph’s κ \kappa were originally designed to measure the reliability of human labeling, thus make assumptions about typical human labeling behavior, and these assumptions may not be applicable to machine generated labels.

arxiv-2411-10961.title: Map-Free Trajectory Prediction with Map Distillation and Hierarchical Encoding
arxiv-2411-10961.creator: Xiaodong Liu, Yucheng Xing, Xin Wang
arxiv-2411-10961.description: Abstract Reliable motion forecasting of surrounding agents is essential for ensuring the safe operation of autonomous vehicles. Many existing trajectory prediction methods rely heavily on high-definition (HD) maps as strong driving priors. However, the availability and accuracy of these priors are not guaranteed due to substantial costs to build, localization errors of vehicles, or ongoing road constructions.

arxiv-2511-07212.title: Matrix-product state skeletons in Onsager-integrable quantum chains.
arxiv-2511-07212.creator: Imogen Camp, Nick G. Jones
arxiv-2511-07212.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Imogen Camp, Nick G. Jones. Matrix-product state (MPS) skeletons are connected networks of Hamiltonians with exact MPS ground states that underlie a phase diagram. Such skeletons have previously been found in classes of free-fermion models. For the translation-invariant BDI and AIII free-fermion classes, it has been shown that the underlying skeleton is dense, giving an analytic approach to MPS approximation of ground states anywhere in the class.

This paper sought to understand the household non-economic welfare of women’s working hours.

pmc-13655330.description: ObjectiveProtoporphyrin IX, a metabolite of 5-aminolevulinic acid (5-ALA), emits red fluorescence.
